title: Agri-Food Processing
breadcrumb: Industries > Agriculture & Food Systems > Agri-Food Processing
meta_description: Food processors live on quality, yield and traceability: intake grading, process yield, food-safety evidence and provenance claims.

blocks.x: The contract behind Agri-Food Processing: signed baseline in week two, working slice by week eight, industrialized controls by week twelve, and evidence flowing to your control owner throughout.

The operating surface here spans Intake grading, Process yield analytics, Lot traceability, Cold-chain monitoring, Provenance claims. Each one is instrumented before anything changes: baseline numbers first, then the working slice, then the measured delta at the gate.

blocks.title: Governed lakehouse pipeline — Agri-Food Processing
blocks.note: Contracts between stages are enforced at the boundary, so schema drift fails loudly in minutes instead of quietly in a quarter.

blocks.x: Every component in Agri-Food Processing has a contract, a version and a named owner. When something drifts, the ticket goes to a person, not to a committee — that is what the reference architecture is for.

items: We treat Intake grading manual as a symptom with a cause — the diagnosis traces it to the decision or the contract that produces it.
We treat Yield opaque as a symptom with a cause — the diagnosis traces it to the decision or the contract that produces it.

Traceability slow shows up in the first conversations with every team we meet in this space; the design gate assigns it an owner and a countermeasure.
When Cold chain unverified is the pain, the baseline audit usually confirms it is structural, not personal — the fix is designed for the system, not the people.
We treat OT estates exposed as a symptom with a cause — the diagnosis traces it to the decision or the contract that produces it.
Tested, documented models with lineage exposure — the transform layer your analysts can actually read.
A single governance plane over tables, models and notebooks — access your auditors can replay.
Data age treated like uptime — a budget, an owner and an alert when it slips.
Open table formats underneath everything we build, so your data never belongs to a vendor.
Line data streamed with the tags that matter, ready for the twin and the OEE math.
Safety results joined to lots and suppliers — traceability that works the day you need it.
Temperature integrity tracked from dock to shelf, with excursions raised as events, not discovered as losses.
Field operations data joined to yield and weather — agronomy argued with numbers.
Spend per query attributed to the team that wrote it — the meter everyone can see.
Breakage restored and measured — the repair clock starts at alert, not at someone noticing.

blocks.x: Failure modes & the guards we ship

items: Metric anarchy — guarded because one certified semantic layer owns definitions — dashboards that shadow it lose endorsement and budget
Cost creep — per-team chargeback with query tags; untagged compute is quarantined at the queue level
Silent schema drift: producer contracts fail loudly at ingest; downstream models refuse to build on drifted sources; the guard is part of the first slice, not a hardening phase

blocks.x: How we help — five priority capabilities

items: Strategy through production operations — models evaluated, retrieval grounded, cost per answer owned.
Pipelines, governance and products on a lakehouse contract — reports that reconcile, lineage you can trace.
Permissioned networks, credentials and provenance — digital trust regulators can inspect.
From sensor data to actuation — industrial IoT fabrics, twins and vision that close the loop.
Identity-first security for people, machines and models — detection, response and audit in one program.

blocks.x: The engagement pattern for Agri-Food Processing: diagnose, prove, industrialize, compound. Each gate reviews evidence with your named owners, and each gate can stop the program.
